info.title: OneNexus Central Auth Service — Customer API
info.description: Customer-facing JSON RPC operations under `/api/*` and authenticated account self-service under `/account/*`. OAuth 2.1 / OIDC protocol endpoints under `/connect/*` are documented separately by their respective specs and the OIDC discovery document at `/.well-known/openid-configuration`.

post.summary: Updates selected profile fields for the current human user.
post.description:
The user and tenant are derived exclusively from the validated access
token. This operation currently supports only `displayName` and
never accepts a user or tenant identifier.

post.summary: Idempotently assigns one role to a user or service client.
post.description:
The assignee and role must belong to the caller's tenant. Repeating the
same request does not create a second assignment; inspect
`created` to tell whether CAS created it on this call.

post.summary: Removes one direct role assignment using its current state token.
post.description:
First obtain the assignment with `ListRoleAssignments`, then send
its `stateToken`. CAS rejects a stale token so an administrator
cannot remove a relationship that changed after it was displayed.

post.summary: Lists direct assignments by exactly one role or assignee filter.
post.description:
Provide exactly one of `roleUri` or `assignee`. Use the
returned `before` or `after` value unchanged to navigate
pages; do not send both cursors in one request.

post.summary: Compiles and idempotently attaches one tenant- or platform-managed policy to a role.
post.description:
A direct attachment makes the policy available whenever the role is
evaluated. Repeating the same request preserves the existing
relationship and returns `created: false`.

post.summary: Detaches one policy from one role using the relationship state token.
post.description:
Get the attachment first with `ListPolicyAttachments` or
`ListRolePolicies`, then provide its `stateToken`. This
protects against deleting a relationship that changed concurrently.

post.summary: Lists roles to which one policy is directly attached.
post.description:
The response contains the direct policy-to-role relationships, not the
users or service clients that inherit access through those roles. Use
the returned cursors for paging.

post.summary: Lists tenant- and platform-managed policies directly attached to one role.
post.description:
This returns only direct attachments. A policy inherited by another
mechanism is not included. Use the returned cursors for paging.

post.summary: Validates and publishes new tenant-managed policy content.
post.description:
Creates a policy in the caller's tenant after validating its document.
A rejected response includes safe diagnostics and creates no usable
policy. Reuse the same `X-Nx1-Idempotency-Key` when retrying a timed-out call.

post.summary: Lists one page of policies visible to the caller's tenant.
post.description:
Returns the tenant's own policies and platform-managed policies that
are available to that tenant. Send at most one returned cursor in the
next request to move backward or forward through the result set.

post.summary: Gets one policy's content without its role attachments.
post.description:
Use this before editing a policy to obtain its current
`contentStateToken`. Attachments are managed separately with the
policy-to-role APIs.

post.summary: Updates only the content of an existing tenant-managed policy.
post.description:
Send the `contentStateToken` returned by the latest read or
successful write. CAS rejects stale updates rather than overwriting a
concurrent change. Platform-managed policies cannot be edited here.

post.summary: Deletes one unattached tenant-managed policy.
post.description:
Remove every direct role attachment before deleting a policy. Send its
current `contentStateToken` so CAS can reject a delete based on an
out-of-date view. Platform-managed policies cannot be deleted here.

post.summary:
Deletes one unreferenced tenant authorization role. Direct grants,
workload bindings, and policy attachments must be removed explicitly
before deletion; CAS never cascades those relationships.
post.description:
Remove every direct user, service-client, workload, and policy
relationship first. CAS does not cascade deletion, which prevents a
role from disappearing unexpectedly from an access configuration.

post.summary: Idempotently creates one tenant authorization role.
post.description:
Role names are case-sensitive ASCII letters and digits. The role is
scoped to the caller's tenant; creating an existing role with the same
name succeeds and returns `created: false`.

post.summary: Updates the optional human-readable description of one tenant role.
post.description:
Send a description of at most 200 characters. Omit it or send
`null` to clear the current description. Role names and URIs are
immutable.

post.summary: Lists authorization roles in the caller's tenant.
post.description:
Results are ordered by role name. The returned `roleUri` is the
stable identifier to use when assigning roles or attaching policies.

post.summary: List the S3 IAM roles provisioned in the caller's tenant account.
post.description:
CAS derives the tenant from the access token; this request cannot list
another tenant's S3 roles. Each result includes the role's trust and
inline permission policies for display in tenant administration tools.

401.description: Caller is not authenticated or has no parseable subject.

post.summary: Assume an S3 role in the caller's tenant account and return temporary credentials.
post.description:
CAS authorizes the requested role before issuing credentials. Use the
returned access key, secret, and session token for S3 requests until
`expiration`; never persist or share the temporary secret.

401.description: Caller is not authenticated or has no parseable subject.

400.description: The supplied S3 role name is not a canonical resource-ID segment.

403.description: Caller is not permitted to assume the requested S3 role.

404.description: Tenant not S3-provisioned, or the role does not exist.

503.description: CAS cannot evaluate the request, or RGW is unreachable.

post.summary: List OAuth service clients owned by the caller's tenant.
post.description:
CAS derives the tenant from the access token. The response includes
client identifiers and registered public keys, never private keys.

post.summary:
Create a tenant-owned service client with its first browser-generated
public assertion key.
post.description:
Generate the key pair in your application or browser and submit only
the public JWK. CAS returns the `clientId` needed at the token
endpoint; it never receives or stores the corresponding private key.

post.summary: Add an additional public assertion key to a service client.
post.description:
Use this to rotate a client key without interrupting the old key. CAS
accepts at most three public keys per service client; retain the
private key outside CAS.

post.summary: Revokes one public assertion key from a service client.
post.description:
The final key cannot be removed. Disable the service client when its
only key is compromised.

post.summary: Disables a service client so it cannot obtain new access tokens.
post.description:
The operation is idempotent. Already-issued short-lived access tokens
retain their normal expiry; disabling prevents subsequent token issuance.

post.summary:
Admin invites a user into their own tenant and triggers the invite
email.
post.description:
CAS derives the tenant from the caller's access token. The user stays
pending until they redeem the emailed invitation and set a password.

200.description:
User created; invitation queued. Body is
    CreateUserResponse.

401.description:
Caller is not authenticated, or the
    authenticated principal no longer maps to a known user
    (`type=https://onenexus.cloud/errors/unauthenticated`).

409.description:
A user with that email already exists in the
    caller's tenant (`type=https://onenexus.cloud/errors/already-exists`) or the caller's tenant
    is not active (`type=https://onenexus.cloud/errors/failed-precondition`).

post.summary: Re-sends an invitation to a pending member in the caller's tenant.
post.description:
CAS derives the tenant from the authenticated caller. Tenant roots and
users in other tenants cannot be targeted through this operation.

post.summary: Lists users in the authenticated caller's own tenant.
post.description:
CAS always lists the caller's tenant; do not send a tenant identifier.
Results include root and member users. Send one returned cursor at a
time to move backward or forward through the list.

post.summary: Redeems an invitation, sets a password, and activates the account.
post.description:
This endpoint does not require an access token. It accepts the
invitation details delivered by email, and an invitation can be used
only once. On success, follow `loginUrl` to sign in.

400.description:
Token invalid/expired, password fails complexity
    rules, or userId unknown. We conflate
    token-invalid and user-unknown to prevent enumeration.

userId.description:
UUID of the invitee. Read from the invite URL's
    `userId` query parameter by the portal.

token.description:
Invite token from the URL's `token` query parameter. Bound to
the user's ASP.NET Identity SecurityStamp at generate-time; verified
via `UserManager.VerifyUserTokenAsync`.

password.description:
Initial password chosen by the user. Subject to the Identity
password-complexity rules configured in
IdentityServiceCollectionExtensions.

tenantId.description: Owning tenant's UUID v7 primary key.

email.description: Email address that was just confirmed.

loginUrl.description:
Suggested next URL for the portal to navigate to — the login form,
with the tenant slug pre-filled so the user only has to type the
email + password.
